stemBlocks.value: Calculate the value of V, where V = π((R − r²)/2 ÷ (R + r)), given R = 22.8, r = 7.50 and π = 3.14.
Think first: Build the answer from the inside out: square r first, then the numerator, then the division, and multiply by π last.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p061-q01 from workbook page 61.

solutionSteps.instruction: Evaluate the numerator R − r² and halve it.

strategyBlocks.value: Substitute the given values, evaluate the top of the fraction, divide by (R + r), then multiply by π.

whyThisWorks.value: Indices are evaluated before subtraction, which is why r is squared before it is taken from R. The bracket containing the division must be completed before π multiplies it, so π is the very last operation. Because r² is much larger than R here, the numerator is negative and so is V - the arithmetic is sound, and a negative value is simply what this substitution produces.

commonErrors.misconception: Working out (R − r)² instead of R − r².
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Working out (R − r)² instead of R − r².

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying by π too early, before the division by (R + r).
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying by π too early, before the division by (R + r).

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing only −33.45 by 30.30 and forgetting the ÷ 2.

examTip.value: Do not round in the middle of a chain of operations - keep the full decimal on your calculator and round only the final answer.
